support_address_confirmation.source: Direct owner confirmation in this task
support_address_confirmation.limits: This confirmation does not verify other aliases, processor deletion permissions, request completion or retention periods.

scope: My Vinyl+ account and associated personal data, or selected personal data. A request may cover more than one device or platform. Discogs accounts and store subscriptions remain separate.
policy_boundaries: A public email request path is supported by Google Play's account-deletion guidance, subject to an actual accessible page and an operational deletion process.
This page and email process do not implement Apple's in-app account deletion requirement for a non-regulated app.
No automatic account deletion endpoint was added. The backend has separate identity stores and processor operations, not a single existing complete deletion function.

details: Use the existing support inbox. Confirm whether the request covers all My Vinyl+ data or selected data, and which platforms or devices were used.
Accept requests without requiring the user to reinstall the app, provide a password, or cancel a subscription.
Explain that My Vinyl+ cannot delete a Discogs account or independently held Apple or Google records.
Set a case-specific expected completion time after identifying the systems involved. Do not promise an unverified universal retention or deletion period.

Record the receipt date, applicable legal response deadline and responsible operator. For UK data protection requests, the normal response deadline is one calendar month; check lawful identity-verification or extension rules and explain any permitted extension within the original deadline. A case-specific estimate must not replace the applicable legal deadline.

operator_steps.action: Verify ownership and build a private identity map
details: A public Discogs username or an email alone is not proof of ownership of a My Vinyl+ purchase identity.

Treat the RevenueCat App User ID and Firebase UID as sensitive. The backend documents purchase UUIDs as capabilities. Do not ask users to post them in a public ticket or include them in repository logs.
Use the minimum verified account or purchase evidence needed through a private support exchange. Do not collect raw authentication tokens or full payment details.

Map each verified identity independently: Django account ID, Supabase binding if present, Firebase purchase UID, RevenueCat customer and aliases, notification installation IDs, and any processor-specific analytics identity.
If a record cannot be safely linked to the requester, explain the limit. Never guess that the same Discogs, Google or Apple login represents the same installation identity.
Use the exact verified identities to preview affected rows and processor records. Keep the case inventory outside Git and general logs.
For a Django account, inspect the ORM deletion cascade and any protected/shared shop records before deleting the user.
For a mobile purchase UID, inspect shops.DeviceToken.purchase_id and the SHA-256 uid_hash in FirebaseCustomTokenBinding separately. Mobile installation identity is not automatically a Django account.
Check open support conversations, identifiable analytics or diagnostic records, and any specific contribution or report referenced by the requester.
Review active jobs or clients that could recreate records. Explain that later app use may create new records; do not claim permanent blocking is implemented.
Delete or request deletion only for records confirmed in the case inventory. The capabilities below are separate operations and require separate readback.
Do not use generic table-wide cleanup or expiry jobs as a substitute for an individual request.
Do not mark the request complete while a required processor deletion or failed storage removal is pending.
Read back each affected system and confirm the expected records are absent, or record the processor's pending deletion status.
Check that authentication cannot use the deleted account and that notification registration does not remain active.
Tell the requester what was deleted, what could not be linked, and any specific information retained with its reason and verified retention period.
Minimize the support case after completion. Keep only what the actual support, security or legal process requires, with an explicit recorded reason and expiry where applicable.
Do not claim that backups, anonymous aggregates, store billing history or independently controlled third-party data were individually erased without supporting evidence.

existing_capabilities.capability: The existing Django user model and ORM can delete an exact verified user. UserProfile, wantlist, follows, collector locations, user-owned device tokens and notifications have cascade relationships.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Inspect the actual cascade first, including shop ownership and protected references. Supabase identity and string-keyed records do not disappear merely because a Django user is deleted.

existing_capabilities.capability: revoke_user_refresh_tokens(user) revokes known refresh tokens. Saving is_active=False triggers revocation and blocks Django account authentication.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Do not use QuerySet.update() expecting save signals. Deactivation is a preliminary control, not completed account deletion.

existing_capabilities.capability: SupabaseService.delete_user(verified_supabase_id) already wraps the server-side Admin API.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Resolve the exact UserProfile.supabase_id. Handle owned Storage objects first when applicable. Deletion does not retroactively invalidate already issued stateless access JWTs; account-specific session behavior requires verification.

existing_capabilities.capability: The configured Firebase Admin SDK supports deletion of an exact verified UID and refresh-token revocation.
existing_capabilities.requirements: The current backend verify_id_token calls do not set check_revoked=True. Revocation alone is not immediate invalidation of all issued ID tokens. No current account-deletion orchestration is implemented.

existing_capabilities.capability: An exact DeviceToken queryset can be removed through the Django ORM after inventory. The existing installation DELETE route only deactivates registrations.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Deactivation or DeviceToken.retire() retains a row and is not erasure. Include all verified purchase UID and installation rows.

existing_capabilities.capability: FirebaseCustomTokenBinding is keyed by the SHA-256 of the exact purchase UID.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Keep this separate from Django and Firebase user deletion. Current clients may mint or recreate an identity later; there is no deletion tombstone or cross-device stop signal.

existing_capabilities.capability: The dashboard and customer APIs provide customer deletion.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Inspect aliases and both app stores. Customer deletion does not cancel the underlying store subscription; later restore or purchase activity can recreate customer data. Verify the intended customer, not only an email or Discogs username.

existing_capabilities.capability: RecognitionSubmissionStorage.remove(paths) removes private objects. Existing cleanup deletes metadata only after storage deletion succeeds.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Use exact, verified contribution identifiers. Current stored submissions have no direct account or purchase UID field. Do not infer ownership from an album, timestamp or photo alone, and do not run expiry cleanup with an artificial date to erase unrelated contributions.

existing_capabilities.system: String-keyed votes, public reports and administrative references
existing_capabilities.capability: DescriptionVote.voter, PublicReleaseReport.contact_email and PremiumOffer purchase-ID fields can hold attributable information outside account foreign-key cascades.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Review exact verified matches and existing service/admin invariants. Do not alter publication state, aggregate counters, running offer cursors or other users' records through a blanket user-delete assumption.

existing_capabilities.capability: Processor and support deletion must be performed using the identity and controls actually available for each service.
existing_capabilities.requirements: Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics, PostHog, TelemetryDeck, AdMob and support email do not all share the RevenueCat UID. Confirm the processor-specific identifier and deletion control; report unlinked or anonymous data honestly. Deleting Firebase Auth does not by itself erase these systems.

processor_identity_limits.capability: Deletion uses the exact Firebase installation ID. Google documents deletion of FID-associated service data within 180 days.
processor_identity_limits.limit: This does not delete Google Analytics data. The Firebase UID, purchase UID and installation ID are different identifiers.

processor_identity_limits.capability: submitUserDeletion accepts supported property-specific identifiers, including an app instance ID or configured user ID.
processor_identity_limits.limit: Resolve the actual Analytics property and identifier. Do not substitute a RevenueCat customer ID or Firebase Auth UID without evidence of a configured mapping.

processor_identity_limits.capability: deleteCrashReports supports reports associated with a user ID previously set through the Crashlytics SDK.
processor_identity_limits.limit: No Crashlytics setUserId call was found in the inspected Android app source. Purchase identity therefore cannot be assumed to locate these reports.

processor_identity_limits.capability: Server-side data deletion requests can target an actual distinct ID.
processor_identity_limits.limit: The app uses an anonymous installation identity, never a Discogs account identifier. PostHog.reset() rotates or unlinks local identity; it does not erase server data. Resolve the deployed project and distinct ID before requesting deletion.

processor_identity_limits.capability: The vendor documents anonymized identifiers and retained analytics when an account closes.
processor_identity_limits.limit: No per-user erasure operation or reliable mapping from purchase identity was verified. Do not promise individual erasure of anonymous aggregates.

android_sdk_disclosure_inventory.scope: Source-backed inventory for the inspected feature/premium-passes worktree. It is not a completed whole-app Play Data safety declaration or proof of the currently distributed APK.
minimum_categories_beyond_ads: Purchase history: RevenueCat provides purchase functionality and analytics; transaction records are not ephemeral.
User IDs: Firebase custom-token authentication uses the app purchase identity. This does not by itself establish email, phone number or real-name collection.
Device or other IDs: Firebase installations, Crashlytics installation identifiers and Google Analytics app instance or advertising identifiers.
App interactions: Analytics sessions, screen views and purchase events, plus the app's custom analytics events.
Crash logs and diagnostics: Crashlytics reports, sessions and handled errors. No Firebase Performance Monitoring dependency was observed.
Approximate location: Already required for Ads; Google Analytics also documents coarse location derived from masked IP information.
collection_controls: The app analytics preference defaults to true and gates its custom transport facade.

Release startup independently enables automatic Crashlytics collection. No Firebase Analytics collection-disable or consent call was found in the inspected source. Do not label all analytics collection optional solely because Settings has an analytics switch.

PostHog is created only for Release when its key and host are nonblank. It has person profiles, session replay, automatic screen and lifecycle events, deep-link capture and automatic error capture disabled; the app sends explicit events.
TelemetryDeck receives custom events, navigation, errors and an anonymized installation identity. Anonymization does not mean no collection occurs.
App Check with Play Integrity processes integrity, license and attestation information for fraud prevention and security.
unverified_before_publication: The exact distributed release, enabled processors, generated PostHog key presence and host. Do not copy or publish credentials while checking.
Whole-app encryption in transit across every actual destination. Vendor transport assurances do not prove the app's configurable PostHog host or every other integration uses HTTPS.
All non-SDK app and backend flows, collection purposes, sharing exceptions, mandatory versus optional collection, deployed retention and the usable account-deletion process.
The final category and handling answers for every applicable SDK version. Vendor disclosure pages describe current SDK behavior and need reconciliation with the distributed release.

known_source_behavior: General backend retention settings are configurable. Zero may retain a table indefinitely. Source defaults are not proof of production settings or successful job execution.
Recognition cleanup removes private storage bytes before metadata and records failures for retry.
Public Release cleanup applies seven-day raw-record and thirty-day aggregate thresholds. Hourly scheduled cleanup is not a strict maximum age if jobs fail, run late or exhaust their budget.
not_verified: Production backup expiration and restore procedures.
General retention execution outside the verified Public Release cleanup.
Processor and support-inbox per-user retention or legal holds.

production_read_only_check.report_cleanup_scope: Clears contact_email, source_address_hash and permission_to_follow_up. Explanation, category, review outcome and audit reason/actor history remain. No report-content/review-history expiry was found.
production_read_only_check.limits: A point-in-time scheduler and aggregate check does not guarantee future job success or cover infrastructure logs, backups, support mail or other processors. No row identifiers, report text or other customer contents were returned.

remaining_engineering_gap.automatic_account_deletion: There is no existing complete function covering Firebase, Django/Supabase, RevenueCat, analytics identities and local state. Adding a single wrapper around SupabaseService.delete_user would not delete a mobile app account.
safe_endpoint_requirements: Verified ownership and recent authentication appropriate to each identity.
Idempotent per-system progress and retry after external processor failures.
Session invalidation and prevention of unintended immediate client re-registration.
Both native clients must start deletion, handle completion, remove local identity and stop background registration.
Focused integration tests with non-production identities, including partial failure and retry.
remaining_engineering_gap.apple_status: Existing iOS Delete account goes to Discogs. This separate app-account deletion gap remains open.
remaining_engineering_gap.play_status: The local request page is not a live deletion URL until deployed and checked. The Data safety declaration remains incomplete.
remaining_engineering_gap.public_retention_readiness: Narrow Public Release cleanup settings and current overdue checks are verified. Complete support, backup and processor retention inventory remains unverified. Do not generalize the Public Release thresholds or claim store compliance.
remaining_engineering_gap.existing_privacy_policy: The fulfillment audit corrected inherited unsupported absolutes as well as processor disclosures. Corrected copy does not establish a working cross-service deletion process; publication remains held pending the release gates.

fulfillment_audit.scope: Claims on the deletion request page and privacy policy, including inherited Public Release and cookie promises. Not a certification of every marketing claim or legal compliance.
supported: The owner confirmed on 2026-10-20 that website@myvinyls.app receives mail and is monitored by them. The manual request intake address is verified.
The source contains distinct per-system deletion capabilities listed below. These require verified identities, operator permissions and independent readback.
Production Public Release cleanup is scheduled hourly and a completed run plus aggregate-only overdue checks were verified.
The ordinary website loads GoatCounter and Ahrefs; appearance preference is stored in browser local storage. The separate Public Release renderer also reads that preference.
corrected_public_claims: Replaced the unconditional cross-service deletion promise with a manual request, identity verification and response process. Do not call this completed account closure.
Explained Android local removal, the iOS Discogs account link, persistent iCloud Keychain purchase identity and possible recreation on later use.
Replaced the seven/30-day maximum guarantees with the verified scheduled cleanup settings and precise application-table scope.
Named the reporter contact fields cleared after 90 days; disclosed that report explanation and review history have no automatic expiry.
Made the report form conditional on availability; submission stores a report for manual review and does not automatically suppress content.
Removed immediate children-data deletion, universal cookie controls, inferred consent merely by using the app, and the blanket restriction on all provider processing purposes.
Disclosed ordinary website analytics and functional local storage; narrowed advertising choice wording to supported versions, region and consent status.
release_gates: Rehearse a request using a controlled disposable identity across every relevant system, including processor permissions, identity verification, failure handling and readback. Do not use an existing customer for testing.
Record retained categories and actual retention periods for support, backups and applicable processors. No general verified retention inventory currently exists.
Do not describe this page as a working store-compliant account-deletion service until the request process can be fulfilled. Native account-closure gaps remain open.
fulfillment_audit.durable_closure_gap: The iOS purchase UUID survives logout/reinstall in synchronizable Keychain. Startup signs into Firebase with it and syncs RevenueCat purchases. The backend has no deleted-identity check and does not check revoked Firebase ID tokens. Server-only deletion can therefore be undone by subsequent app activity.
minimum_closure_changes: An authenticated deletion state checked by token issuance and authenticated writes, with session revocation and a deliberate rejoin path.
Both clients must stop background registration and purchase synchronization for a deleted identity, clear the relevant local identity, and handle closure across devices.
Integration coverage with disposable identities for partial failures, retries, old tokens and attempted automatic recreation.
fulfillment_audit.intake_evidence: The existing iOS Settings support email includes premiumStatus.supportUserId (RevenueCat appUserID) in FeedbackConfiguration.swift. This can help locate a purchase identity privately; an ID alone is not proof of ownership. That email uses feedback@myvinyls.app, whose delivery/monitoring is also unverified.
fulfillment_audit.validation_limits: Source audit and read-only production settings, scheduler metadata and aggregate counts. No provider deletion or disposable-account rehearsal, no customer deletion, no production mutations.
